blocks.title: Monitoring and Security Tools exam shortcuts
items: Need to correlate logs from many sources → SIEM
A SIEM centralizes telemetry and applies correlation and alerting.
Example: VPN, firewall, and authentication logs are correlated into one incident.
Sensitive data is leaving by email/USB → DLP
DLP focuses on preventing unauthorized data disclosure.
Example: An upload containing SSNs is blocked.
Network device sends event without being polled → SNMP TRAP
A trap is an unsolicited device notification.
Example: A switch sends an interface-down trap.
Need traffic metadata, not packet contents → NETFLOW
NetFlow summarizes network conversations.
Example: Analysts identify which host sent the most outbound traffic.
Need secure configuration reference → BENCHMARK
Benchmarks define recommended settings.
Example: A server is compared against a CIS benchmark.
Need standardized automated configuration/vulnerability checks → SCAP
SCAP supports machine-readable security assessment content.
Example: A compliance tool uses SCAP content to test settings.
Need local endpoint telemetry → AGENT
An installed agent can observe host activity directly.
Example: EDR runs as an endpoint agent.
Cannot install software on target → AGENTLESS
Use remote or API-based collection.
Example: A cloud service is monitored through APIs.
blocks.example: Focus on whether the scenario is asking for visibility, detection, containment, validation, or a specific monitoring tool.

questions.q: A company wants to centralize logs from firewalls, servers, and authentication systems and correlate them into security alerts. Which tool is best?
questions.explanation: A SIEM centralizes and correlates logs and can generate alerts.

questions.q: A control blocks an employee from emailing a file containing Social Security numbers outside the company. Which tool is this?
questions.explanation: DLP is designed to prevent unauthorized disclosure or movement of sensitive data.

questions.q: A switch automatically sends an interface-down message to the monitoring system without being polled first. Which mechanism is this?
questions.explanation: SNMP traps are unsolicited event notifications from network devices.

questions.q: An analyst wants to know which systems communicated, over which ports, and how much data was transferred, without capturing full packet contents. Which tool is best?
A compliance tool automatically checks system configurations using standardized machine-readable security content. Which technology is most relevant?
questions.explanation: SCAP supports automated vulnerability, configuration, and compliance assessment.

questions.q: A server is compared against a CIS secure-configuration standard. What is the standard called?
questions.explanation: Benchmarks provide recommended secure configuration standards.

questions.q: An EDR product installs software directly on each endpoint to collect local telemetry. Which approach is this?
questions.explanation: Agent-based monitoring uses software installed on the target.

questions.q: A cloud platform is monitored through its API because software cannot be installed on the service. Which approach is this?
questions.explanation: Agentless monitoring collects information without installing local software.

questions.q: A security team wants to identify missing patches and known system vulnerabilities. Which tool is most appropriate?
questions.explanation: Vulnerability scanners identify known flaws, missing patches, and misconfigurations.
